title: Pascal's Triangle
corePattern: Dynamic Programming - Iterative Row Construction via Additive Recurrence
interviewTips: Clarify input range: numRows = 0 vs 1-indexed? Constraints say 1 <= numRows <= 30, confirm expected return for 1 is [[1]].
Trade-off to discuss: binomial formula nCr recomputes each cell independently vs DP reuses previous row - O(n^3) vs O(n^2) time.

Edge-case tip: first and last element of every row are always 1, inner elements need bounds check j-1 >=0 and j < prev size; watch int overflow for larger n (C(29,14) fits 32-bit but larger would not).

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force via Binomial Coefficient (nCr)
approaches.intuition: Each entry of Pascal's Triangle is a binomial coefficient: row i col j equals C(i, j). So we can build the triangle by directly computing the combinatorial value for every position independently using the multiplicative formula.
approaches.theory: C(n,k) = n! / (k! * (n-k)!) can be computed iteratively as res=1; for i in 0..k-1: res = res*(n-i)/(i+1) using symmetry k = min(k, n-k) to halve work. We loop i=0..numRows-1 and j=0..i and fill ans[i][j]=C(i,j). This is correct because Pascal's Triangle is exactly the table of binomial coefficients, but it recomputes overlapping factorials from scratch.

timeComplexity.explanation: There are O(n^2/2) cells and each nCr(i,j) takes O(min(j, i-j)) = O(n) multiplications/divisions, so total O(n^3). If factorial is recomputed naively per cell it is even worse.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Output stores 1+2+...+n = O(n^2/2) integers. Extra auxiliary space is O(n) for current row, O(1) besides output if not counting result.

edgeCases: numRows=30 max constraint still fits 32-bit int, use long during intermediate multiplication to avoid overflow
Symmetry optimization r = min(r, n-r) needed to keep loop short and avoid overflow

approaches.name: Approach 2: Optimal Iterative DP Row-by-Row
approaches.intuition: Each interior value is the sum of the two values above it. Instead of recomputing combinations, build rows top-down reusing the previous row: pad with 1s on both ends and fill middle as sum of upper-left and upper.
approaches.theory: Pascal recurrence: T[i][j] = T[i-1][j-1] + T[i-1][j] for 0<j<i, with T[i][0]=T[i][i]=1. This is DP with optimal substructure - row i depends only on row i-1. By induction from base row [1], all rows are correct. Each cell computed once in O(1), giving optimal time for explicit triangle generation.

timeComplexity.explanation: Total cells is sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (i+1) = n*(n+1)/2, each computed in O(1) addition. This is optimal since output size itself is O(n^2).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Output triangle uses O(n^2) space. Extra working space is O(n) for current row, O(1) if not counting output.

edgeCases: numRows=1 returns [[1]] - loop for j in range(1,i) skipped
numRows=2 returns [[1],[1,1]] - second row has no interior computation
Large numRows beyond 30 would overflow 32-bit int, need long; current constraints safe
